key_insight: MoRight disentangles object motion from camera viewpoint and enforces motion causality, so user-specified actions trigger coherent physical reactions in the scene instead of merely displacing pixels.
problem_solved: Existing motion-controlled video models entangle camera and object motion and fail to produce causal, physically plausible interactions—users cannot independently control viewpoint and expect other objects to respond coherently to driven actions.
method: Disentangled representation: separate latent channels for object action control and camera viewpoint to enable independent manipulation.
Causal dynamics module: learns object–object interaction dynamics so user actions induce coherent reactions (not just pixel shifts).
Viewpoint-aware synthesis and multi-term training (reconstruction + causality-consistency + viewpoint-consistency) to produce physically plausible, controllable videos.
impact: Makes controllable video synthesis more reliable and useful for interactive applications (animation, simulation, robotics) by enabling independent viewpoint control and causally correct scene behavior—improving realism and downstream utility.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: two-stream latent (action vs viewpoint) feeding a causal dynamics module and viewpoint-aware renderer
Before/after comparison: baseline output vs MoRight on the same control input showing causal reactions vs pixel displacement
Frame sequence storyboard: an action (e.g., push) causing other objects to respond under multiple camera viewpoints
Training flowchart: losses and supervision signals (reconstruction, causality-consistency, viewpoint-consistency)
paper_authors: Shaowei Liu, Xuanchi Ren, Tianchang Shen, Huan Ling, Saurabh Gupta
